description: Where in the instance a failure is reported. Every failure has a location — the root's is the empty JSON Pointer — and the corpus pins how each one is rendered, including the RFC 6901 escapes and the locations the current rendering cannot distinguish.

cases.name: a failure of the whole instance is reported with no location
cases.description: The location is the empty JSON Pointer, which both wrappers render by printing nothing.

cases.name: a missing top-level member is reported against the root object
cases.description: A missing member is reported against the object that lacks it, which for a top-level requirement is the root.

cases.name: a failure inside a member is reported at that member's pointer
cases.description: A failure inside a member is reported at that member's pointer.

cases.name: an array element's location is its index
locations compose down through objects and arrays alike
the member named "" is reported as though the whole instance had failed
cases.description: RFC 6901 gives the member named "" the pointer "/" — a different location from the root, whose pointer is "". Both wrappers use "/" as their sentinel for the root, so this failure is rendered as though it were a failure of the whole instance.

defect.summary: The member named "" is reported as a root failure, because "/" is used as the root sentinel.
defect.should: The root is the empty pointer and should be represented as a first-class value, not as the string "/"; the member named "" should render at "/" and be distinguishable from it.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: 'not a number' is not of type 'number'

cases.name: a member name containing "/" goes unescaped, so its pointer reads as a nested member
cases.description: RFC 6901 escapes "/" in a member name as "~1", so the member "a/b" of the root object has the pointer "/a~1b" — distinct from the member "b" of the member "a".

defect.summary: jsonschema-validate joins path segments with "/" without escaping, so "a/b" renders as "/a/b" and is indistinguishable from a nested member. ajv-validate escapes correctly.
defect.should: Both legs should render RFC 6901 pointers with ~0 and ~1 escapes, and should therefore agree.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: /a/b: 'not a number' is not of type 'number'

cases.name: a member name containing "~" goes unescaped, so its pointer does not address it
cases.description: RFC 6901 escapes "~" in a member name as "~0".

defect.summary: jsonschema-validate does not escape "~", so the rendered pointer is not a valid JSON Pointer for this member.
defect.should: Both legs should render RFC 6901 pointers with ~0 and ~1 escapes, and should therefore agree.

jsonschema-validate: INVALID: /a~b: 'not a number' is not of type 'number'

cases.name: each failure gets its own line and its own location
